doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Loving music but hating the music business and the road
summary: Marty distinguishes music from the business, recalls jam sessions, and tells how bus reading hurt his eyes.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You’ve got the road in your blood I guess.

No not really. You know what I always say, like I remember once when I was very disappointed about playing club dates, like weddings and things like that, bar mitzvah’s and that type, I said I think I’m going to give it up and — she says, “you going to quit the music business?” No she says, “I thought you like music?” I said, “Honey, I love music. I hate the music business. There’s a difference.

Because playing music, this is what happens with a lot of musicians. That’s why these two guys formed this thing, so they can get musicians their royalties. Because guys, they love to play. Look how many times you go to the jam session, and the boss in the club loved it because he paid for a trio and got 18 guys on the bandstand. You know I played a million places like that where I’d have a trio and guys come in from all over the place. One guy brought his vibraphone and set them up on the front of the bandstand. One guy had a baritone, he put his case on the table and chair in the dining room. I says, “man, don’t do that, put it on the bandstand.” He says, “where?” But the bosses of course, they loved it. They had all these free musicians playing. Great. So anyway, but my wife has taken a lot from me all these years. But like I say I don’t mind the traveling, I don’t like

the road I guess is what it is. It’s the buses and falling asleep in the bus. That’s how I started wearing glasses. I never wore glasses. Because the guys in the bus would be sleeping and I’d have the little light on with a book and the thing going up and down like that. And after I while I said man I can’t see the words anymore. So I lost my sight on the buses from reading.
